metaData.originalTitle: Fine-Tuning NVIDIA Cosmos Predict 2.5 with LoRA/DoRA for Robot Video Generation
metaData.title: Fine-Tuning NVIDIA Cosmos Predict 2.5 with LoRA/DoRA for Robot Video Generation
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This guide provides a step-by-step walkthrough for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of NVIDIA Cosmos Predict 2.5 using LoRA and DoRA to generate synthetic robot manipulation videos, including data preparation, training, inference, and evaluation.
metaData.summary: This article from the NVIDIA team on the Hugging Face Blog presents a comprehensive, practical guide for fine-tuning the Cosmos Predict 2.5 world model for robot video generation. It addresses the challenge of expensive real-robot data collection by proposing a scalable alternative: generating synthetic trajectories with a fine-tuned video world model. The core of the guide focuses on parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) using LoRA and DoRA, which inject small trainable adapters into the frozen 2B-parameter model, making it feasible on a single GPU. The article details the entire pipeline: setting up the environment, preparing the GR1-100 dataset, implementing the training loop with rectified flow loss, running inference with the fine-tuned adapter, and evaluating results using Sampson Error and LLM-as-a-Judge metrics. Quantitative results show that fine-tuning for 100 epochs significantly improves temporal stability, physical plausibility, and instruction following. The guide concludes with practical advice on choosing between LoRA and DoRA based on rank and budget, and provides links to the full codebase and further resources.

mainPoints.point: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning with LoRA/DoRA makes adapting large world models like Cosmos Predict 2.5 practical on a single GPU.
mainPoints.explanation: By freezing the base 2B-parameter model and training only small adapter modules, the memory footprint is drastically reduced, and the resulting adapter files are small and portable, enabling flexible domain adaptation.

mainPoints.point: Fine-tuning a world model on robot demonstration data enables scalable generation of synthetic trajectories for downstream robot learning.
mainPoints.explanation: This approach addresses the bottleneck of collecting expensive real-robot data by using the fine-tuned model to generate diverse, physically plausible robot manipulation videos from text prompts and initial frames.

mainPoints.point: The fine-tuned model shows significant quantitative improvements in temporal stability, physical plausibility, and instruction following over the base model.
mainPoints.explanation: Evaluation using Sampson Error and LLM-as-a-Judge metrics confirms that even 100 epochs of training substantially enhances video quality, with the model learning to generate correct robot hands and follow task instructions reliably.

keyQuotes: Training robot policies requires demonstration data, but collecting real-robot trajectories is slow and expensive. Generating synthetic trajectories with a fine-tuned video world model offers a scalable alternative.
LoRA and DoRA inject small trainable adapter modules into the frozen base model, reducing memory requirements while keeping the adapter files small and portable.

Fine-tuning with LoRA and DoRA addresses all three issues: robot hands are out-of-distribution, it does not reliably use the correct hand specified in the prompt, and the generated videos exhibit noticeable jitter.
Training for 100 epochs (~2.5 hours on 8× H100s) is already sufficient to substantially improve all three metrics.
If memory is very tight or adapter file size matters, start with LoRA r=8. If you have budgets and observe training instability with LoRA at low rank, DoRA r=32 is a reasonable alternative.
